title: She left the AI race over her health. Two days later, OpenAI had her back.

content_html:
On Tuesday, Lilian Weng said she was stepping down from Thinking Machines Lab because the job was making her ill. On Wednesday, she was back at OpenAI.

Weng co-founded Thinking Machines Lab with Mira Murati, OpenAI’s former chief technology officer. She is rejoining OpenAI to work on recursive self-improvement, or using AI models to build better AI models, The Information reported.

‘Beyond what my health can sustain’

Her exit note was stark. Weng said she had been ill more often in the past seven months than at any point in her life, and did not name a diagnosis. The “consistent stress and workload,” she wrote, had pushed her “beyond what my health can sustain physically,” Business Insider reported.

She said she tried to rest while the lab sprinted to ship Inkling, its first open-weight model, but felt guilt. She had weighed a narrower role and decided it was not a fit. She wanted something “more predictable” and “scoped,” while staying in AI. “The future worth building is human,” she wrote on X.

The role she took is not the calmer one

What she returned to is not obviously that calmer job. Recursive self-improvement, using AI to build better AI, is one of the most consequential and contested problems in the field. It is the frontier the whole race is sprinting toward.

There is an irony in it. A researcher who just hit her own human limits is going to work on machines that are meant to have none. Her recursive self-improvement brief puts her at the very edge of the technology.

She is not the only one

Weng’s health exit fits a pattern. Fidji Simo stepped back from a top OpenAI role this month after a flare-up of a chronic illness. In January, xAI co-founder Greg Yang moved to an advisory role after a Lyme disease diagnosis. He said he needed to “go founder mode” on his health.

The people stepping away tend to sit one level below the chief executive. Some Silicon Valley AI teams run “996” schedules, 9am to 9pm, six days a week. The bosses at the top mostly stay put, and the race does not slow down.

A lab losing its founders

The move thins Thinking Machines further. By May, 13 of the lab’s 42 founding members had left, including three of its six co-founders, as Meta and OpenAI dangled huge pay packages. “We’ll miss you,” Murati wrote in reply. “I’m glad that you’re putting your health first.”

Read one way, this is a person choosing her health, and a former employer welcoming her back. Read another, it is the AI race proving it can pull even its burned-out talent straight back in. Weng wanted a slower lane. She got the fastest problem in the field.

content_html_zh:
周二，Lilian Weng 表示，她将从 Thinking Machines Lab 辞职，因为这份工作让她生病了。 周三，她回到了 OpenAI。

翁先生与 OpenAI 前首席技术官 Mira Murati 共同创立了 Thinking Machines Lab。 据 The Information 报道，她将重新加入 OpenAI，致力于递归自我改进，或者使用人工智能模型来构建更好的人工智能模型。

“超出了我的健康所能承受的范围”

她的退出说明很鲜明。 翁说，过去七个月里她生病的次数比她一生中任何时候都多，但她没有透露诊断结果。 据《商业内幕》报道，她写道，“持续的压力和工作量”已经让她“超出了我的健康所能承受的范围”。

她说，当实验室全力运送 Inkling（第一个开放式重量模型）时，她试图休息一下，但感到内疚。 她权衡过一个较小的角色，并认为它不适合。 她想要一些“更可预测”和“范围更广”的东西，同时留在人工智能领域。 “未来的价值在于人类，”她在 X 上写道。

她所扮演的角色并不平静

她回去的工作显然并不是那么平静。 递归自我改进，即使用人工智能构建更好的人工智能，是该领域最重要和最具争议的问题之一。 这是整个种族正在冲刺的前沿。

这其中有一种讽刺。 一位刚刚达到人类极限的研究人员将在原本没有人类极限的机器上工作。 她的递归自我完善简介使她处于技术的最前沿。

她不是唯一一个

翁先生的健康退出符合一种模式。 Fidji Simo 在慢性病发作后于本月辞去了 OpenAI 最高职位。 今年 1 月，xAI 联合创始人格雷格·杨 (Greg Yang) 在诊断出莱姆病后担任顾问。 他说他需要在健康方面“进入创始人模式”。

离职的人往往比首席执行官低一级。 一些硅谷人工智能团队实行“996”时间表，上午 9 点到晚上 9 点，每周工作六天。 顶层的老板大多保持原样，比赛并没有放缓。

失去创始人的实验室

此举进一步削弱了思维机器的规模。 到 5 月，由于 Meta 和 OpenAI 悬而未决的巨额薪酬，实验室 42 名创始成员中有 13 人离开，其中包括 6 名联合创始人中的 3 名。 “我们会想念你的，”穆拉蒂回复道。 “我很高兴你把健康放在第一位。”

从某种角度来看，这是一个选择自己健康的人，也是一位欢迎她回来的前雇主。 另读另一篇文章，人工智能竞赛证明了它甚至可以将已经倦怠的人才直接拉回来。 翁想要一条较慢的车道。 她是该领域最快解决问题的人。
